principle: Colour decides the scope bucket. Measurement type decides the unit. Nothing else in the markup is read by the machine, so nothing else may be relied on to carry meaning.
why_profiles: v1.0 was inferred from a single site/civil sheet. The Harbor Freight interior sheet uses several of the same colours for different scopes - blue is concrete flatwork on a site plan and the tenant strip-out footprint on an interior plan. One flat legend cannot hold both without producing wrong quantities, so the legend is scoped by discipline and the extractor is told which profile to read.

match.method: nearest legend colour by Euclidean RGB distance, within the selected profile
match.on_miss: emit as UNMAPPED with needs_review=1 - never guess a bucket

units.length: LF - Bluebeam /PolyLine or /Line with a dimension intent

confidence_levels.confirmed: Cross-checked against a priced bid line or an explicit plan note.
confidence_levels.probable: Consistent with the drawing and with the other profile, but not independently confirmed.
confidence_levels.unconfirmed: Observed in a real markup, meaning not yet established. Extracts with needs_review=1 until Shawn confirms it.

rate_card_gaps.note: Structure footprint / limits-of-work demolition. Closest existing is exterior_demo (SF, wall and cladding), which prices a different operation.
Chain link fence and gate removal. Currently absorbed into lump site items.
Buried utility line removal / cap. Production varies hugely with depth and surface above - may need a depth band rather than one rate.
Abatement containment. Must never be folded into a demolition rate - different licence, different crew, different liability.
Linear abatement (pipe insulation, mastic, duct wrap).

Full tenant strip-out priced against lease-space SF. Harbor Freight gives a first real data point: $44,950 base bid over 11,885.24 SF = $3.78/SF for fixtures + abandoned equipment + electrical + doors + lay-in ceiling + light fixtures + all floor finishes.
Interior slab / quarry tile / setting bed removal. Harbor Freight bundles 1,357.1 SF of this with 379 SF of trench sawcut at $25,912.50 combined, so the two cannot be separated from this bid alone.
